name: Infantile Onset Panniculitis with Uveitis and Systemic Granulomatosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Infantile Onset Panniculitis with Uveitis and Systemic Granulomatosis

criteria.description: Histopathologically confirmed lobular panniculitis with granulomatous inflammation
Clinical or ophthalmological evidence of uveitis (anterior, intermediate, or posterior)
Evidence of systemic granulomatous inflammation affecting organs such as lymph nodes, liver, or lungs
Onset of symptoms within the first 2 years of life
Exclusion of infectious causes of granulomatous inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (panniculitis, uveitis, and systemic granulomatosis) with onset in infancy and exclusion of infectious etiologies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including dermatology, ophthalmology, and pathology.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Granulomatous lobular panniculitis confirmed by skin biopsy
searchTerms: inflammatory skin nodules confirmed by biopsy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systemic granulomatous inflammation involving multiple organs

searchTerms: subcutaneous nodules or thickened skin areas
skin bumps or plaques under skin

common.symptomName: Anterior uveitis with eye redness and photophobia
searchTerms: eye redness with pain and light sensitivity
red, painful eyes sensitive to light

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss or failure to thrive

searchTerms: pus layer in front eye chamber
white blood cell accumulation in eye
fluid buildup in anterior eye chamber

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
Negative infectious workup including tuberculosis and fungal infections
imaging: Chest radiograph or CT showing pulmonary granulomas or nodules
Ultrasound or MRI demonstrating lymphadenopathy and organomegaly
genetic: No known specific genetic mutation identified; likely multifactorial or autoinflammatory etiology
other: Skin biopsy showing lobular panniculitis with non-caseating granulomas

distinguishingFeatures: Typically presents in older children or adults
More common pulmonary involvement without panniculitis
Less frequent panniculitis and uveitis combination
Positive microbiological cultures or PCR for infectious agents

redFlags: Rapid progression of uveitis leading to vision loss
Development of systemic organ failure due to granulomatous infiltration
Failure to respond to immunosuppressive therapy
references: Orphanet: Infantile Onset Panniculitis with Uveitis and Systemic Granulomatosis, ORPHA:251304
